text:
Good morning. Today is Sunday, October fourth, and here is your political news briefing.

First, the news from home, where the ruling New Patriotic Party, or N P P, has concluded its national delegates conference in Kumasi.

Story one. Graphic Online and MyJoyOnline report that John Boadu has staged a political comeback to be elected the new National Chairman of the N P P, winning forty-eight point five percent of the votes. Meanwhile, Justin Frimpong Kodua retained his position as General Secretary with a massive majority, and former Member of Parliament Mavis Hawa Koomson was elected as the new National Women's Organiser.

Story two. According to reports from The Ghana Report and Three News, N P P delegates approved fourteen constitutional amendments, including a major change that officially makes the party's presidential candidate the leader of the party. The People's National Convention, or P N C, has criticized this move, warning that making the flagbearer the party leader could weaken internal democracy.

Story three. MyJoyOnline and Three News report that former Vice President Doctor Mahamudu Bawumia has called for immediate unity, demanding that all internal camps dissolve to form one united N P P for the twenty-twenty-eight elections. Doctor Bawumia urged the party to begin work immediately, promising to involve defeated candidates in the campaign, while also taking the opportunity to criticize the opposition N D C's policies.

Now, around the world.

Story four. France Twenty-Four and Africa News report that conflict has intensified in Yemen, where Houthi rebels claimed to have struck an oil facility near Riyadh, prompting Saudi forces to launch twenty-six retaliatory strikes on the capital, Sanaa. The United Nations reports that at least one hundred and fifty thousand people have fled their homes due to the escalating violence, which is worsening the country's humanitarian crisis.

Story five. From South America, Deutsche Welle and France Twenty-Four report that Brazil is on the eve of a highly competitive presidential election, with polls showing incumbent President Lula da Silva and challenger Flavio Bolsonaro nearly tied. The campaigns wrapped up in the key state of Sao Paulo as both sides made a final push to win over undecided voters before Sunday's vote.

You can now open Dad News and ask for more about any story by its number.
